Photograph: Facebook Greece Athens suitcase death: suspect admits hiding body but denies murder Police are focusing on Elisabeth-Jane Ross’s final hours in hope of discovering motive for her killing Helena Smith in Athens Mon 3 Aug 2026 15.36 EDT Last modified on Mon 3 Aug 2026 21.30 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Greek authorities are investigating what may have motivated a 26-year-old Afghan man to kill a Scottish charity worker found dead in a suitcase in an abandoned building in Athens last month. Inquiries have focused increasingly on Elisabeth-Jane Ross’s last few hours alive and police believe they hold the key to revealing why the 38-year-old was targeted. On Sunday the suspect, identified as Sharif Ahmadzai, was accused of intentional homicide after three days of questioning. He will appear before an investigating magistrate to be formally charged on Wednesday. George Kalliakmanis, the honorary president of the police officers’ association in Athens, told the Guardian the homicide division was now intent on discovering the motive behind “the murder” because the Afghan was continuing to deny any role in it, although he had confessed to hiding Ross in a suitcase. “He has admitted to carrying her body to the site. Police have CCTV footage of him doing this on the night of 16 July. He has also confessed to withdrawing €10,000 from ATMs using credit cards that belonged to her. But he has denied murder which police do not believe,” Kalliakmanis said. The Afghan, a professional boxer in the lightweight division, is believed to have arrived in Greece via the island of Lesbos as a child refugee at the height of Europe’s migration crisis 10 years ago. View image in fullscreen Sharif Ahmadzai and his wife, US citizen Alaina Hall. She is said to have played a ‘significant role’ in the investigation. Photograph: Twitter/X He has been quoted as telling police he discovered Ross’s lifeless body in the first floor flat of an apartment block he helped manage in Exarchia, a bohemian district in downtown Athens popular among leftists, foreigners and NGOs. Ahmadzai, who married a US citizen and devout Christian, Alaina Hall, in 2023, had keys to the flat where their own refugee solidarity group, Love Every Nation, regularly met. Investigators have confirmed that Ross, a friend of Hall’s with similar volunteering experience and religious views, had moved to the apartment on 10 July after staying with Greek friends when she arrived in the Athens from Edinburgh on 26 June. Her last telephone call was made from her mobile phone on the night of 15 July – three days before her body was discovered by a homeless man in an abandoned building in Kypseli, about two miles away. Two possible scenarios in the run up to Ross’s death were being studied, police said. “We believe there was a confrontation,” said one source. “But was that spurred by Ross discovering the Afghan rummaging through her things and stealing her credit cards, or was it a case of sexual assault or the Briton spurning his advances?” View image in fullscreen Sharif Ahmadzai arrived in Greece via the island of Lesbos as a child refugee. He has been accused of intentional homicide. Photograph: Twitter/X Forensic scientists believe Ross was “likely asphyxiated” after an initial on-site postmortem, which showed there were no evident signs of injuries on her body. However, the autopsy was also deemed inconclusive because of advanced decay. Further toxicological tests and analysis of vital organs are expected to determine the exact cause of death in the coming days. Hall, who met Ahmadzai on Lesbos, is widely described as having played a “significant role” in the investigation. After allegedly becoming suspicious of Ahmadzai’s movements – and newfound wealth, the result of making cash withdrawals with Ross’s credit cards – she reportedly contacted the police, handed over cash he had given her and moved into a hotel. Adding to the mystery that has engulfed the inquiry, Ross’s phone was used for several days after her death, with text messages sent to family and friends. The messages were described as “deliberately misleading” by police, who believe they were sent in a bid to delay Ross being declared missing. One spoke of her “need to be alone”. “The Afghan’s partner was very helpful,” said Kalliakmanis. “From the day the victim was identified the investigation faced several challenges but thanks to the homicide division being so thorough they cracked it.” Police, who collaborated with the UK’s National Crime Agency and the Scottish service, combed through CCTV footage from cameras in the area where the suitcase was found and from banks where cash withdrawals were made before identifying the suspect. Photograph: Stefan Rousseau/PA View image in fullscreen Heathrow airport’s July passenger total was 1.5% down compared with the same month last year. Photograph: Stefan Rousseau/PA Heathrow airport Heathrow says need for expansion ‘clear’ as it loses title of Europe’s busiest airport West London airport reports 7.86 million passengers in July, compared with 8.15 million for Istanbul Business live – latest updates PA Media Tue 11 Aug 2026 04.02 EDT Last modified on Tue 11 Aug 2026 08.12 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Heathrow airport said “the case for expansion has never been clearer” after it was overtaken as Europe’s busiest airport by Istanbul. Figures published on Tuesday showed 7.86 million passengers passed through Heathrow’s four terminals in July, compared with Istanbul’s 8.15 million. Heathrow’s passenger numbers for July fell, while London Stansted and Manchester both had record traffic for the month. Annual figures from the trade body Airports Council International show Heathrow was Europe’s busiest airport from 1996 to 2019. EasyJet agrees to £5.7bn takeover by US private equity firm Read more The UK’s biggest airport, located west of central London, lost that position in 2020 amid coronavirus travel restrictions before regaining it in 2023 and holding the title since then. Heathrow’s July passenger total was 1.5% down compared with the same month last year, while the Turkish hub recorded a 2.3% increase. The US-Israel war on Iran has affected Heathrow’s passenger traffic. Numbers on Middle East routes were down 20.2% year on year in July. Heathrow continues to operate its two runways at near full capacity, and is seeking government permission to build a third. An expansion proposal by the airport’s owners would enable it to accommodate 150 million passengers a year - up from about 85 million in 2025. The airport said: “Heathrow is operating at capacity. The case for expansion has never been clearer, as Heathrow was overtaken in July by Istanbul airport as the busiest hub in Europe. “Our plans will ensure the country gets the infrastructure it needs to stay competitive and will deliver all-important economic growth.” The comparison, however, may not fully bolster Heathrow’s case. The airport was only opened in late 2018 and built on a brand new site away from the city and residential neighbourhoods, gradually replacing the existing Ataturk airport as the main international hub. It has a vastly bigger footprint and is able to operate 24 hours a day. The Turkish boom also owes much to its location near the Gulf, which has become the crossroads of international air travel. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Business Today Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning Preview latest after newsletter promotion The transport secretary, Heidi Alexander, launched a consultation on the renamed Heathrow expansion national policy statement in June, setting out the conditions needed if the project is to be given the go-ahead. The then chancellor, Rachel Reeves, said at the time she was determined to get “spades in the ground” for the third runway in the current parliament, and for it to be built by 2035. Andy Burnham, who sacked Reeves, has previously expressed concerns over Heathrow expansion, stating the plans divert infrastructure investment “away from the north and traps it in London”. Heathrow’s chief executive, Thomas Woldbye, said summer was “off to a flying start” but “we want to go further” by “growing our route network and passenger offering”. “Expanding Heathrow will help ensure the UK remains home to Europe’s leading hub and continues to benefit from the trade, investment and tourism that increased connectivity will bring,” he said. London Stansted said it had recorded the busiest month in the airport’s history in July, welcoming 3.1m passengers, a 6.3% increase year-on-year. Manchester also had a record July, serving 3.4m passengers. https://www.energy-storage.news/econergy.text: News Econergy signs financing agreements for 150MW solar-plus-storage project in Romania By April Bonner August 17, 2026 Europe Connected Technologies , Grid Scale Technology , Business LinkedIn Twitter Reddit Facebook Email Econergy also stated that Părău 2 secured the largest capacity award in Romania’s contracts for difference (CfD) mechanism, 125MW at US$57.18/MWh for 15 years from commercial operation, expected in late 2027 or early 2028. Image: Pexels/Ch Jawad Independent power producer (IPP) Econergy has signed financing agreements for its Părău 2 solar and energy storage project in Brașov County, Romania. Announced 14 August, Econergy signed the agreements for the 342MW solar PV and 150MW battery energy storage system (BESS) project with a six-lender consortium comprising the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), the Black Sea Trade and Development Bank (BSTDB), Exim Banca Românească S.A., NLB d.d., OTP Bank Plc and Banca Comercială Intesa Sanpaolo România, for an aggregate financing package of approximately EUR€229 million (US$265 million). Econergy also stated that Părău 2 secured the largest capacity award in Romania’s Contracts for Difference (CfD) mechanism, 125MW at US$57.18/MWh for 15 years from commercial operation, expected in late 2027 or early 2028. Romania launched its second CfD round in 2025 . The first round was more than three times oversubscribed with 1.6GW of bids made for PV capacity. Părău 2 is currently under construction and expected to enter commercial operation in late 2027 or early 2028. Once operational, Econergy claims the the project is expected to increase Romania’s renewable electricity generation capacity, reduce greenhouse gas emissions and support the reliability of the national power system. Our colleagues at PV Tech reported in October 2025 that Chinese engineering firm Shanghai Electric had signed an engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) agreement with Econergy for Părău 2 . Shanghai Electric also worked on phase one of the project which was commissioned in 2024 . Romania has relatively recently become one of Europe’s most active BESS markets. Activity accelerated with gigawatt-level announcements , led by Enery’s US$530 million financing for its 761MW solar and 1GWh-plus BESS Ogrezeni project, set to become one of Europe’s largest hybrid projects. In July, London-headquartered BESS developer Alcemi acquired 1,200MWh and 1,100MWh BESS projects in Romania . The same month, Energy-Storage.news reported on project developments in the country from Pan-European battery storage and renewables platform Aukera, Romanian energy solutions provider ENEVO Group, and PPC Renewables Romania, part of the Greek state-owned Public Power Corporation (PPC). ESN spoke with Joshua Murphy, head of energy storage for Econergy , at the Energy Storage Summit 2026 in London in February. https://telex.hu/after/2026/09/01/budape.text: Menü Kereső A főváros és a korábbi szervezők sem táncolnak az új Budapest Parádé ötletétől After Bulizók a 2005-ös Budapest Parádén – Fotó: Isza Ferenc / AFP Bányász Dorka Több mint 20 év után újra megrendezik a Budapest Parádét – ezzel büszkélkedett az a szerkesztőségünkhöz is eljutott közlemény vasárnap, amit a Budapest Parkban tartott Parádé Remember másnapján küldtek ki. A tervezett esemény hivatalos, mesterséges intelligenciával készített képeket használó weboldala szerint a bulit az SSD Parádé Nonprofit Kft. 2027 augusztusára szervezi az Andrássy útra, ahol a kétezres évek elején megszokott eseményekhez hasonlóan körülbelül 30 kamion vonulna fel magyar és külföldi fellépők szettjeivel. A szervezők a bejelentéssel valójában kampányt indítottak, hogy minél többen támogassák a rendezvényt, a szervezéssel járó költségek egy részét ugyanis a támogatóktól érkező bevételekből finanszíroznák. A Facebook-eseményen jelenleg 17 ezer érdeklődő van, és a szervezők elmondása szerint már több mint száz, többek között rendezvénytechnikai vagy kamionos felajánlás érkezett hozzájuk. A rendezvény sorsa azonban elég bizonytalan, és minél több érintettel beszéltünk, annál több lett a kérdés. A fővároshoz nem jutott el részletes terv A vonulásra például még nem adta áldását a főváros, ugyanis a Budapest név használata engedélyköteles, azt csak főpolgármesteri engedéllyel használhatja rendezvény, ezt az engedélyt az eredeti, 2000 és 2006 között rendezett parádé szervezőinek is minden évben igényelniük kellett. Elértük az idén júliusban alapított SSD Parádé egyik alapítóját, Száler Gábort, aki kérdésünkre azt mondta, hogy többször keresték a Főpolgármesteri Hivatalt és a Fővárosi Önkormányzatot is, ahonnan minden alkalommal azt a választ kapták, hogy dolgoznak az ügyön, de a tényleges folyamatoknak szerinte nem volt nyomuk. A főváros viszont kérdésünkre azt írta, hogy augusztus 10-én a névhasználati engedély iránti kérelem eredménytelenül zárult. Az eljárásban a Fővárosi Önkormányzat szerint a szervezőcég nem indokolta meg megfelelően a névválasztást, és nem derült ki, hogy a rendezvényen kívül milyen egyéb céges tevékenységekhez használnák még a Budapest Parádé elnevezést. A tervezett esemény tartalma teljesen ismeretlen maradt, a kérelmező cég semmilyen részletes szakmai tervet vagy konkrét elképzelést nem mutatott be a jövőbeli rendezvény megvalósításáról – írta válaszában a főváros. A Budapest Parádé hivatalos Facebook-eseménynél a szervezők azt is közölték, hogy eredetileg nem SSD Parádé Nonprofit Kft., hanem Budapest Parádé Nonprofit Kft. néven akartak céget alapítani, de ezt a Fővárosi Önkormányzat szintén a „Budapest” név használata miatt nem engedélyezte. A Budapesti Rendőr-főkapitányságot is megkérdeztük az eseményről, ahonnan azt a választ kaptuk, hogy korábban érkezett hozzájuk ilyen bejelentés, azonban azt a bejelentő végül visszavonta. Száler szerint ha demonstrációként jelentik be az eseményt, az a gyülekezési törvény hatálya alá esik, amit csak 30 nappal a rendezvény megtartása előtt lehet bejelenteni. Ez az opció pedig egy ilyen nagyságú és előkészületet igénylő eseménynél nem jó megoldás. Ilyenkor jön szóba az, hogy a Fővárosi Önkormányzattól bérlik ki a helyszínt, amit a cég a nonprofit működése miatt szeretne ingyen megkapni, de egyelőre erre sem kaptak engedélyt. A korábbi szervezők nem álltak be az esemény mögé Száler még áprilisban indította el a védjegyek megszerzésének folyamatát, de a Szellemi Tulajdon Nemzeti Hivatalának adatbázisa alapján egyelőre csak az látszik, hogy a Budapest Parádé logójának bejegyeztetése folyamatban van. A szervezőcég alapítója kérdésünkre azt mondta, hogy mivel a Budapest Parádét eredetileg a Sziget szervezte, így felvette a kapcsolatot Gerendai Károllyal is. Száler elmondása szerint Gerendai támogatja az esemény újraindítását, de a projekt lebonyolításában sem ő, sem a Sziget nem vesz részt. Száler elmondása szerint megkereste Kurucz Gergelyt, a Parádé Remember esemény szervezőjét és Lobenwein Norbert fesztiválszervezőt is, aki az eredeti Budapest Parádé egyik rendezője volt, de eddig nem mutattak komolyabb érdeklődést az irányába. A Sziget részéről megerősítették, hogy tényleg megkereste őket a cég, ekkor irányították a korábbi események szervezőihez Száleréket. Lobenwein Norbert is annyit tudott megerősíteni a kérdésünkre, hogy keresték az ügyben, de konkrét egyeztetésig aztán nem jutottak. Szerinte a Budapest Parádéhoz tartozó domén a Sziget tulajdona maradt, ez lehet a magyarázat arra, hogy az új weboldal a .com kiterjesztést kapta. A szervezőt a Rendszerbontó Nagykoncert is inspirálta Száler szerint az eseményre felajánlott támogatásokkal, adományokkal átláthatóan számolnak el, és ha az idei rendezvény megszervezése után is marad tartalékuk, akkor azt a következő évi rendezvénybe fektetik. Száler szerint az esemény szervezésében alapvetően a berlini Love Parade inspirálta, de nagy hatással volt rá a Polgári Ellenállás Rendszerbontó Nagykoncertje , és az áprilisi választás éjszakáján tapasztalt népünnepély is. Az esemény közleménye szerint környezetbarát rendezvényként hoznák vissza a Budapest Parádét, és az a tervük, hogy a felvonuló járművek elektromos hajtásúak lesznek, valamint a hang- és fénytechnika is zöldárammal fog működni. A Budapest Parádét eredetileg 2000 és 2006 között, általában augusztus végén rendezte a Sziget, az eseményen kamionokat indítottak az akkori DJ-k, klubok, rádiók, tévécsatornák és magazinok. A csúcsidőszakban akár 700 ezren is összegyűltek a Budapest Parádén, de az esemény végül 2007-ben már elmaradt, mert az akkori szervezők szerint nem jött össze elég pénz a szponzoroktól. A parádétól 2006 után az a VI. kerületi önkormányzat is elfordult , akkor jelentették be, hogy nem támogatják többé a rendezvényt. Kövess minket Facebookon is! Követem! Friss az Afteren

Photograph: Wai Lee Michael Ho/SOPA Images/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen Police respond to the scene after three people were found dead inside a home in San Diego, California, on 16 September 2026. Photograph: Wai Lee Michael Ho/SOPA Images/Shutterstock San Diego San Diego police investigate case of family of three found fatally shot in home Navy veteran David Voight, his wife, Amy, and their child were found dead as relatives report Voight was suffering from PTSD Dani Anguiano Fri 18 Sep 2026 14.45 EDT First published on Fri 18 Sep 2026 13.31 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Authorities are investigating what led to the tragic case of a family who was found fatally shot in their San Diego area home on Wednesday morning. The San Diego police department identified the family as Amy Voight, 54, and David Voight, 56, and the couple’s 13-year-old daughter. The family died of gunshot wounds, police said, and investigators found a weapon in the residence. Gerald Austin, Amy Voight’s father, told the San Diego Union-Tribune that his son-in-law had served in the navy as a officer in Iraq and Afghanistan, while his daughter worked with the Naval Criminal Investigative Service as a digital forensic examiner. He went on to say that his daughter adored David Voight, and that he believed the violence was driven by David Voight’s suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Mary Austin, Amy Voight’s mother, said she had noted that David Voight’s symptoms had recently become more severe and that she and her husband urged their daughter to seek help for the veteran. “You could visibly see there was something really wrong,” Mary Austin told Fox 5 . “He was fidgety. You could tell.” Gerald Austin said his daughter had sought help for her husband in recent days, but they were unable to receive services because they did not have an appointment, allegations the Department of Veterans Affairs denied. The Department of Veterans Affairs said it could not comment on the case, citing privacy concerns, but that “what’s being alleged regarding VA services is not accurate”. “All VA healthcare facilities offer same-day mental healthcare to all veterans who need it,” said Quinn Slaven, the VA press secretary. The couple and their daughter were discovered by a concerned neighbor on Wednesday morning, and all were pronounced dead at the scene. The county medical examiner’s office will conduct autopsies to determine the cause and manner of death, police said in a statement. Seven out of every 100 veterans will experience PTSD in their lives, according to the VA. The rate is higher among veterans who served in Iraq and Afghanistan at 29%. Deployment significantly increases the risk of PTSD, according to the VA.
